hypothesis: The measured compact 128-thread tile is currently best at 0.00089008 s, while compact 160-, 192-, and 256-thread candidates measured 0.00092808, 0.00092263, and 0.00091997 s. With nine distinct prior programs and no repeats, this candidate tests a new 224-thread CTA/tile between the 192- and 256-thread settings. Each thread still computes one target, and its 224 compact source records use 3,584 bytes of shared memory. The measurements are non-monotonic, so no speedup is assumed.
notes: The kernel stages only source position and mass, processes sources in ascending order, and keeps all CTA threads participating in both barriers, including threads without valid output targets. The 3,584-byte allocation is below the previously valid 4,096-byte compact candidate. The controller should run correctness checks before timing; this candidate has not been measured.
transformations: Set block and items_per_block to 224 so each thread remains responsible for exactly one target and the staged source tile matches the CTA width.
